note.en: Ali ibn Ibrahim glosses these signs of the heavens and the earth as the eclipse, the earthquake, and the thunderbolts [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: شرك طاعة وليس شرك عبادة والمعاصي التي يرتكبون شرك طاعة أطاعوا فيها الشيطان فأشركوا بالله في الطاعة لغيره وليس بإشراك عبادة أن يعبدوا غير الله
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Jafar

text.en: It is a shirk of obedience, not a shirk of worship. The sins they commit are a shirk of obedience: in them they obeyed Satan and so associated another with Allah in obedience to Him. It is not the shirk of worship, that they worship someone other than Allah.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هو الرجل يقول: لو لا فلان لهلكت، و لو لا فلان لأصبت كذا و كذا، و لو لا فلان لضاع عيالي، ألا ترى أنه قد جعل لله شريكا في ملكه، يرزقه و يدفع عنه
narrations.chain: Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is the man who says, 'Had it not been for so-and-so I would have perished; had it not been for so-and-so I would have lost my family.' Do you not see that he has set up a partner to Allah in His dominion, one who provides for him and wards off harm from him?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ذلك رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) و أمير المؤمنين و الأوصياء من بعدهما
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Ahwal, from Salam ibn al-Mustanir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: That is the Messenger of Allah, and the Commander of the Faithful, and the successors after the two of them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Jawad
narrations.arabic: وما ينكرون علي من ذلك فوالله لقد قال الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وآله … فما اتبعه غير علي عليه السلام وكان ابن تسع سنين وأنا ابن تسع سنين
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat

text.en: What do they hold against me in this? By Allah, in what Allah said to His Prophet, none followed him but Ali - and he was nine years old, and I am nine years old.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أو لست تعلم أن الله تعالى لم يخل الدنيا من نبي قط أو إمام من البشر؟ … فأخبر أنه لم يبعث الملائكة إلى الأرض، فيكونوا أئمة و حكاما، و إنما أرسلوا إلى أنبياء الله
narrations.chain: al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his forefathers, from al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad

text.en: Do you not know that Allah has never left the world without a prophet or an imam from mankind? He did not send angels to the earth to be imams and rulers; the angels were sent only to the prophets of Allah.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: يقول الله تعالى حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من قومهم، و ظن قومهم أن الرسل قد كذبوا، جاء الرسل نصرنا
narrations.chain: Tamim ibn Abdillah, from his father, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Jahm

text.en: Allah says: until the messengers despaired of their peoples, and their peoples thought that the messengers had lied to them, Our help came to the messengers.

perspectives.en: Verse 110 sets the commentators debating who 'thought they had been told lies.' The Shia commentators guard the prophets' certainty: the messengers despaired only of their peoples, and it was those peoples who took the messengers for liars - the reading al-Rida gave al-Ma'mun in defence of prophetic infallibility [19]. The Sunni tafsirs hold several readings at once. Aisha too refused any hint that a prophet could doubt his Lord, yet al-Tabari also records, from Ibn Abbas, that the messengers, being human, grew weak and lost hope, supposing the promise of help had failed them [30].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالمراد بالشرك في الآية بعض مراتبه الذي يجامع بعض مراتب الإيمان وهو المسمى باصطلاح فن الأخلاق بالشرك الخفي.

sources.gloss: So the shirk meant in the verse is one of its degrees that coexists with some degrees of faith, and it is what the science of ethics calls the hidden shirk.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: بيَّن سبحانه أنه إنما أرسل الرسل من أهل الأمصار لأنهم أرجح عقلاً وعلماً من أهل البوادي

sources.gloss: He explained that He sent the messengers only from the people of the towns, because they are more sound in reason and knowledge than the people of the deserts.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: تصديق الكتب التي قبله من التوارة، والانجيل

sources.gloss: a confirmation of the books before it, the Torah and the Gospel.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: شرك طاعة وليس شرك عبادة

sources.gloss: a shirk of obedience, not a shirk of worship.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فما اتبعه غير علي عليه السلام وكان ابن تسع سنين وأنا ابن تسع سنين

sources.gloss: None followed him but Ali, and he was nine years old, and I am nine years old.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الكسوف و الزلزلة و الصواعق

sources.gloss: the eclipse, the earthquake, and the thunderbolts.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ألا ترى أنه قد جعل لله شريكا في ملكه، يرزقه و يدفع عنه

sources.gloss: Do you not see that he has set up a partner to Allah in His dominion, one who provides for him and wards off harm from him?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ذلك رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) و أمير المؤمنين و الأوصياء من بعدهما

sources.gloss: That is the Messenger of Allah, and the Commander of the Faithful, and the successors after the two of them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لم يبعث الملائكة إلى الأرض، فيكونوا أئمة و حكاما، و إنما أرسلوا إلى أنبياء الله

sources.gloss: He did not send the angels to the earth to be imams and rulers; the angels were sent only to the prophets of Allah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من قومهم، و ظن قومهم أن الرسل قد كذبوا، جاء الرسل نصرنا

sources.gloss: until the messengers despaired of their peoples, and their peoples thought the messengers had lied, Our help came to the messengers.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: كانوا بشراً ضعفوا ويئسوا

sources.gloss: They were human beings; they grew weak and lost hope.
